known_pitfalls.claim: The tertiary sector does not contribute to production because it does not manufacture goods.
known_pitfalls.correction: Tertiary activities provide services that support production and also include essential services.

known_pitfalls.claim: GDP includes the value of all intermediate and final goods separately.
known_pitfalls.correction: GDP counts final goods and services so that intermediate values are not counted repeatedly.

known_pitfalls.claim: Underemployed workers are not working at all.
known_pitfalls.correction: Underemployed workers may appear employed but work below their productive capacity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Organised and public sector mean the same thing.
known_pitfalls.correction: Organised–unorganised concerns employment conditions; public–private concerns ownership.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Table 2.1 to establish interdependence among sectors.
Use the NCERT wheat–flour–biscuits example to explain final and intermediate goods.
Use NCERT Graphs 1–3 and the Laxmi example to connect production, employment and disguised unemployment.
Use the NCERT Kanta–Kamal comparison for organised and unorganised employment.
Use the NCERT public-sector examples of infrastructure, electricity and the Public Distribution System.
